posts.text: The 'holy shit' moment when I realized agent-browser can control Slack. npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-browser --skill slack
posts.notes: Slack skill for agent-browser via vercel-labs/agent-browser --skill slack. 548K views, 1564 bookmarks. Signals that agent-browser's Electron approach generalizes to any desktop app — Slack being the most impactful because it is central to team workflows. Demonstrates a cheap path to 'let agents work inside chat tools' without API integrations.

posts.text:
New: Autonomous Dogfooding

A skill for agent-browser that uses your app the way your users do

→ Point it at any URL
→ Explores pages, clicks buttons, fills forms
→ Tests edge cases and checks the console
→ Captures repro videos and step-by-step screenshots
→ Outputs a structured report with severity ratings

No test scripts. No manual QA.
posts.notes: Autonomous Dogfooding skill announcement. Agent-driven QA: no test scripts, no manual QA — point at URL and get structured severity report with repro video. 610K views, 6034 bookmarks. Strong E2E testing automation signal.

posts.text:
New: @json-render/react-pdf

You can now go from prompt to PDF with json-render

Same JSON format as the React and React Native renderers, minus state and actions

Just swap the renderer and get a PDF
posts.notes: json-render/react-pdf: prompt-to-PDF via same JSON format as React/React Native renderers. 76K views, 1486 bookmarks. Signals that json-render's component catalog model is render-target agnostic — relevant for agent-generated document pipelines (invoices, reports, contracts).

posts.text: Introducing Generative shadcn/ui for json-render @json-render/shadcn 36 ready-to-use shadcn/ui components. Add to your catalog. Ship Generative UI faster.
posts.notes: Generative shadcn/ui for json-render: 36 ready-made shadcn components that can be dropped into the json-render catalog. Important because shadcn is already the de facto component system for AI-built UIs — this makes json-render the path of least resistance for any team on the stack.

posts.text: Exactly one month ago, we launched and open sourced agent-browser. Today, it has crossed 500,000 weekly downloads. This momentum belongs to the community. Every issue opened, every pull request merged and every bit of feedback shared has pushed the project forward.
posts.notes: agent-browser milestone: 500K weekly downloads one month post-launch. Community milestone post. Signals massive adoption of Vercel's agentic browser automation tool.
